steps.name: DESeq2 interaction model: condition x time
caveats: The interaction coefficient is a difference of two differences; at 3 replicates per cell its power is low. A gene absent from the interaction list is NOT shown to have the same treatment effect at both time points

A gene-level Salmon matrix without length offsets can mis-call a gene whose isoform usage shifts between conditions or time points
If T1S1 flagged a sample, note its influence on the affected genes rather than removing it silently — removal would leave a cell with n=2
steps.context: 12,000 genes x 12 samples of raw integer counts from Salmon, gene symbols as row identifiers, single batch, human cell line. 2 conditions x 2 time points (t0, t1) x 3 replicates. The research question is exactly the interaction term. steps.question: Which genes show a treatment effect that differs between t0 and t1 (the condition:time interaction), and what is the treatment effect within each time point separately?

steps.description: Fit one DESeq2 model on all 12 samples with design ~ condition + time + condition:time. Set the reference level of condition and of time explicitly (time reference = t0; state the chosen condition reference in the output) rather than relying on alphabetical ordering. Pre-filter minimally: keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 3 samples (the smallest group size). Let DESeq2 estimate median-of-ratios size factors inside the model — do not pre-normalize. Run the Wald test on the interaction coefficient as the PRIMARY result. Then extract, as named contrasts on the same fit, the simple treatment effect at t0 (the condition main effect at the reference time) and the simple treatment effect at t1 (main effect plus interaction). Shrink log2 fold changes with ashr for every contrast — the t1 simple effect is a combination of coefficients, which apeglm cannot take. Report both the unshrunken and shrunken log2FC with lfcSE for each gene. Apply BH adjustment with independent filtering at alpha 0.05 WITHIN each contrast, and state that FDR control holds per contrast, not across the three. Plot the unadjusted p-value histogram of each contrast before trusting its adjustment, and describe its shape. Report the number of genes with NA p-values from the Cook's-distance outlier flag separately from those removed by independent filtering (with 3 replicates per cell DESeq2 flags rather than replaces outliers). State the expected power: compute, from the observed dispersion and library depth, the fold change detectable at 80% power with n=3 per cell, and note that the interaction standard error exceeds that of a main effect. steps.name: Preranked GSEA per contrast

steps.context: Human data, so hallmark is the first pass and Reactome plus WikiPathways are the further collections. Three contrasts from T1S2. The significant gene list from the interaction contrast is expected to be small at n=3 per cell, which is precisely why the ranked method on the full list is used instead of an over-representation test.
steps.question: Which biological processes show a time-dependent treatment response (interaction contrast), and how do the processes engaged by treatment at t0 differ from those at t1?

grounding.reason: Preranked fgsea on the full tested list per contrast (R-0107, R-0045, R-0104); disputed rank metric R-0108 resolved in favour of the DESeq2 Wald statistic per R-0099; human collection order hallmark then Reactome and WikiPathways per R-0048, R-0098, R-0165; ORA declined per R-0103 given the expected small interaction list.

constraints: Reference data needed: human hallmark gene sets, human Reactome pathway gene sets, and human WikiPathways gene sets — resolve each against the environment's reference store and record the release of each; do not download anything
Filter the Reactome collection to Homo sapiens before testing — the served pathway file spans multiple species

Use the full ranked list of tested genes; do not run an over-representation test on the significant genes (the interaction list is expected to be far below the ~50-gene threshold at which ORA has any power)
Keep the three collections as three separate result tables; do not merge them into one set list
Set and report the random seed before the permutation test
steps.description: Run fgsea preranked enrichment separately on each of the three ranked lists exported by T1S2 — the condition:time interaction, the treatment effect at t0, and the treatment effect at t1. Ranking metric stated in the output as the DESeq2 Wald statistic, with the reason for the choice
Gene set size window 15-500 applied after intersection with the tested genes and reported
Hallmark, Reactome (human subset) and WikiPathways human run as three separate analyses, results never pooled, each with its collection release stated

steps.question: Taken together, does the treatment effect differ between t0 and t1 — and with what confidence, given 3 replicates per design cell?

grounding.reason: Interaction design report: simple effects beside the interaction contrast with reference levels named (R-0092), power statement at n=3 (R-0094), two-method overlap (R-0042), shrunken and unshrunken effects (R-0085), fit diagnostics (R-0087), enrichment provenance and leading edge (R-0051, R-0105), method-dependence caveat (R-0055), reproducibility record (R-0086).

constraints: Report the interaction contrast and both simple effects together for every reported gene — never the interaction coefficient alone and never a simple effect alone
Name the reference level of condition and of time beside every coefficient table
Rank genes and plot on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit
Do not describe any enriched set as an established mechanism; present sets as hypotheses
Do not soften or omit the power statement to make the result read more strongly
steps.description: Assemble the final report. Answer the research question directly first: state the number of genes with a significant condition:time interaction at padj < 0.05, and whether the evidence supports a time-dependent treatment effect. For each reported gene, give three results side by side — the treatment effect at t0, the treatment effect at t1, and the interaction contrast — with the reference level of each factor named beside the table, since coefficient meaning depends on it. Unshrunken log2FC, shrunken log2FC and lfcSE present for each contrast; ranking and plots use the shrunken value
MA plot, dispersion plot and p-value histograms placed before the gene tables
DESeq2/edgeR intersection reported as the robustness statement
Enrichment reported with collection name and release, ranking metric, universe, size window, tool version, and per-set leading-edge genes

plan.title: Treatment x time interaction DE in 2x2 bulk RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question — does the treatment effect differ between t0 and t1 — is an interaction question on a 2 (condition) x 2 (time: t0, t1) design with 3 replicates per cell (12 samples, 12,000 genes, gene-symbol rows, Salmon-derived raw integer counts in counts.csv; sample table in metadata.csv with condition, time, time_hours). The plan therefore fits one DESeq2 model with design ~ condition + time + condition:time on the full 12-sample matrix and takes the interaction coefficient as the primary result, with the simple treatment effects at t0 and at t1 reported beside it (an interaction contrast alone does not say whether treatment acts at either time point, and a simple effect alone does not say whether the effects differ).

Order: sample-structure QC first (blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes, coloured by condition and time) because with n=3 per cell a single aberrant sample can drive the interaction; then the minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=3 samples, the smallest group size), median-of-ratios size factors inside the model, the Wald test on the interaction coefficient, ashr shrinkage (the simple effect at t1 is a combination of coefficients, not a single one, so apeglm cannot serve it), BH within each contrast at alpha 0.05, and a p-value histogram check before trusting the adjustment. An edgeR quasi-likelihood fit of the same design runs as a second method so the report can give the DESeq2/edgeR overlap rather than one tool's list.

Power is the dominant caveat and is stated explicitly rather than worked around: an interaction coefficient is a difference of two differences, so its standard error exceeds that of a main effect at the same replicate count, and 3 replicates per cell detects only a minority of true effects, mostly large-fold-change ones. Thresholds are not loosened to compensate, and absence from the interaction list is not evidence that the effect is the same at both time points.

Enrichment is a preranked fgsea pass on the full tested list ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (stated choice among the disputed metrics; the Wald statistic scales effect by its uncertainty, unlike an unshrunken fold change), run separately per contrast — interaction, treatment effect at t0, treatment effect at t1 — against human MSigDB Hallmark first, then Reactome and human WikiPathways as the further collections with their releases stated. Counts are gene symbols (HGNC), which matches those GMTs directly; the unmapped share is reported. Enrichment is interpretive support, not the answer to the question, so if a collection is missing at run time the step reports which ran and continues.

One data caveat the profile forces: the counts are a gene-level matrix, so the tximport length-offset route the Salmon provenance would otherwise call for cannot be applied — the transcript-level quant.sf files are not among the inputs. The step must state this, since a gene-level Salmon matrix without length offsets can mis-call a gene whose isoform usage shifts.

steps.question: Do the genes called as having a time-dependent treatment effect replicate under a second count model (edgeR quasi-likelihood) fitted to the same ~ condition + time + condition:time design?
steps.description: Fit the same design (~ condition + time + condition:time) to the same filtered count matrix with edgeR: TMM normalization factors, estimateDisp, glmQLFit, and glmQLFTest on the interaction coefficient, plus the two simple-effect contrasts via makeContrasts on the same fit. Apply BH within each contrast at FDR 0.05. Report, per contrast, the number of significant genes from edgeR, the number from DESeq2 (T1S2), and the size of the intersection. Treat the intersection as the high-confidence set and list the method-specific calls as a secondary set naming the method. Do not present the union as the result. Produce a rank-correlation (Spearman) of the two methods' interaction test statistics across all tested genes.
steps.context: Same 12-sample, ~12,000-gene filtered matrix as T1S2. The two count models agree on most genes at these replicate numbers but diverge at low counts and low replication, which is exactly this design's regime, so the overlap is the honest robustness statement.
acceptance_criteria: edgeR QL fit of the identical design and identical filtered gene set completed
Per-contrast significant-gene counts from edgeR, from DESeq2, and their intersection reported in one table
High-confidence intersection set exported for the interaction contrast
Method-specific calls listed separately with the calling method named
Spearman correlation of DESeq2 Wald statistic and edgeR QL statistic across tested genes reported for the interaction contrast
Explicit statement that the union is NOT the reported result
constraints: Use exactly the same gene filter and the same design formula as T1S2 so the comparison is like-for-like
Use TMM normalization factors inside the edgeR model; do not feed pre-normalized values
Report the intersection as the high-confidence set; do not report the union
caveats: Disagreement between the two methods is expected to be largest for low-count genes and is amplified at 3 replicates per cell — a method-specific call is a weaker claim, not a contradiction
Both methods share the same low power for the interaction term; agreement does not remove the power limitation

grounding.reason: Second count model for robustness: edgeR quasi-likelihood on the same design, report the DESeq2/edgeR overlap as the high-confidence set per R-0042; edgeR QL is a permitted method at 2-11 replicates per R-0001.

steps.name: Preranked GSEA per contrast
steps.question: Which biological processes show a time-dependent treatment response (interaction contrast), and how do the processes engaged by treatment at t0 differ from those at t1?
steps.description: Run fgsea preranked enrichment separately on each of the three ranked lists exported by T1S2 — the condition:time interaction, the treatment effect at t0, and the treatment effect at t1. Rank every tested gene by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the `stat` column); this is the stated choice among the disputed ranking metrics, taken because it scales the effect by its uncertainty, unlike an unshrunken fold change, and unlike a signed p-value it does not tie genes at the top of the list. Never threshold the list before the test. Restrict gene sets to 15-500 members after intersecting with the tested genes. Run three collections independently, never merged: human MSigDB hallmark gene sets first, then Reactome pathway gene sets (restricted to Homo sapiens via the pathway index) and human WikiPathways. Row identifiers are HGNC gene symbols, matching these collections directly; report the share of tested genes not present in each collection's symbol space. BH-adjust within each collection and each contrast. Collapse redundant significant sets (fgsea collapsePathways) and report one representative per group with the full table as a supplement. For each significant set, list its leading-edge genes with their gene-level statistics and mark leading-edge overlap between reported sets. State each collection's release beside its results. Summarize which sets are shared between the t0 and t1 contrasts and which are unique, as the pathway-level reading of the interaction.
steps.context: Human data, so hallmark is the first pass and Reactome plus WikiPathways are the further collections. Three contrasts from T1S2. The significant gene list from the interaction contrast is expected to be small at n=3 per cell, which is precisely why the ranked method on the full list is used instead of an over-representation test.
acceptance_criteria: fgsea run on the full ranked list of every tested gene for each of the three contrasts — no pre-thresholding
Ranking metric stated in the output as the DESeq2 Wald statistic, with the reason for the choice
Gene set size window 15-500 applied after intersection with the tested genes and reported
Hallmark, Reactome (human subset) and WikiPathways human run as three separate analyses, results never pooled, each with its collection release stated
Share of tested gene symbols unmapped to each collection reported
BH adjustment applied within each collection and contrast; redundant sets collapsed with one representative per group and the full table kept as a supplement
Leading-edge genes with their gene-level statistics listed for each significant set, with overlaps between sets marked
A comparison of enriched sets at t0 versus t1 versus the interaction contrast, stated as hypotheses
Random seed set and reported for the fgsea permutations
If a collection is absent at run time, the step reports which collections ran and proceeds with the rest rather than failing
constraints: Reference data needed: human hallmark gene sets, human Reactome pathway gene sets, and human WikiPathways gene sets — resolve each against the environment's reference store and record the release of each; do not download anything
Filter the Reactome collection to Homo sapiens before testing — the served pathway file spans multiple species

Use the full ranked list of tested genes; do not run an over-representation test on the significant genes (the interaction list is expected to be far below the ~50-gene threshold at which ORA has any power)
Keep the three collections as three separate result tables; do not merge them into one set list
Set and report the random seed before the permutation test
caveats: Enrichment results depend on the method and the collection; a significant set is a hypothesis for follow-up, not a proven finding
With low interaction power at n=3 per cell, an empty interaction enrichment table is an expected outcome and not evidence that the treatment response is time-invariant
Gene length and expression level bias enrichment on count data; the universe is the tested genes, which removes only the detection component of that bias
A pathway appearing in two collections is one finding tested twice, not two findings

grounding.reason: Preranked fgsea on the full tested list per contrast (R-0107, R-0045, R-0104); disputed rank metric R-0108 resolved in favour of the DESeq2 Wald statistic per R-0099; human collection order hallmark then Reactome and WikiPathways per R-0048, R-0098, R-0165; ORA declined per R-0103 given the expected small interaction list.

steps.name: Integrated interaction report
steps.question: Taken together, does the treatment effect differ between t0 and t1 — and with what confidence, given 3 replicates per design cell?
steps.description: Assemble the final report. Answer the research question directly first: state the number of genes with a significant condition:time interaction at padj < 0.05, and whether the evidence supports a time-dependent treatment effect. For each reported gene, give three results side by side — the treatment effect at t0, the treatment effect at t1, and the interaction contrast — with the reference level of each factor named beside the table, since coefficient meaning depends on it. Include the unshrunken log2FC, the ashr-shrunken log2FC and lfcSE per contrast; rank genes and draw all plots on the shrunken value. Carry forward the MA and dispersion plots and the p-value histograms from T1S2 as fit diagnostics, placed before the gene tables. Report the DESeq2/edgeR overlap from T1S3 as the robustness statement. Report the enrichment results from T2S1 with, for each: the collection and its release, the ranking metric, the universe, the size window, the tool version, and the leading-edge genes of each significant set. State the power limitation prominently: 3 replicates per cell, the fold change detectable at 80% power, the larger standard error of the interaction term, and the explicit statement that a gene absent from the interaction list is not shown to have an equal treatment effect at both time points. Name the enrichment method-dependence caveat. Close with a reproducibility record: sessionInfo, all package versions, the random seeds, and the version of every gene set collection used.
steps.context: Consolidates T1S2 (DESeq2 interaction and simple effects), T1S3 (edgeR replication) and T2S1 (per-contrast GSEA) into one document for a 12-sample, 2x2 human cell line experiment.
acceptance_criteria: Direct answer to the research question stated first, with the interaction gene count at padj < 0.05
Per-gene table giving the t0 simple effect, the t1 simple effect and the interaction contrast side by side, with both factors' reference levels named beside it
Unshrunken log2FC, shrunken log2FC and lfcSE present for each contrast; ranking and plots use the shrunken value
MA plot, dispersion plot and p-value histograms placed before the gene tables
DESeq2/edgeR intersection reported as the robustness statement
Enrichment reported with collection name and release, ranking metric, universe, size window, tool version, and per-set leading-edge genes

Explicit power statement: 3 replicates per cell, detectable fold change at 80% power, larger interaction standard error, and that absence from the interaction list is not evidence of a time-invariant effect
Enrichment method-dependence caveat stated
Reproducibility record with sessionInfo, package versions, seeds and gene set collection versions stored with the results
constraints: Report the interaction contrast and both simple effects together for every reported gene — never the interaction coefficient alone and never a simple effect alone
Name the reference level of condition and of time beside every coefficient table
Rank genes and plot on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit
Do not describe any enriched set as an established mechanism; present sets as hypotheses
Do not soften or omit the power statement to make the result read more strongly
caveats: This is an underpowered interaction design (n=3 per cell); a null interaction result is uninformative about equality of effects, not evidence for it
A cell line at two time points also carries a time effect independent of treatment — the time main effect should be reported so the interaction is read against it

grounding.reason: Interaction design report: simple effects beside the interaction contrast with reference levels named (R-0092), power statement at n=3 (R-0094), two-method overlap (R-0042), shrunken and unshrunken effects (R-0085), fit diagnostics (R-0087), enrichment provenance and leading edge (R-0051, R-0105), method-dependence caveat (R-0055), reproducibility record (R-0086).
